statement: W&B's unit is the run: one unit of computation, treated as the atomic element of a project.
quote: A run is a single unit of computation logged by W&B. You can think of a W&B Run as an atomic element of your whole project.

statement: A W&B run is addressed by id, name, configuration and state, and those are the fields the SDK hands back.
locator: §What are runs? (paragraph after the init example)
quote: wandb.init() returns a wandb.Run object that contains properties of the run, such as its ID, name, configuration, and state.

statement: W&B separates the metric series from the run's summary: final or aggregate values live somewhere else than the logged history.
quote: Unlike metrics that change over time, summary values typically represent a final or aggregate result.

statement: The W&B object that carries a version is the artifact, and it is defined by its relation to the runs that consumed or produced it.
quote: Use W&B Artifacts to track and version data as the inputs and outputs of your W&B Runs

statement: An artifact's type is a label the logger chooses, and it defaults to unspecified — no taxonomy is imposed by the vendor.
quote: If you do not specify a type, it defaults to unspecified.

statement: MLflow's unit is also a run, and it means one execution of the training code.
quote: MLflow Tracking is organized around the concept of runs, which are executions of some piece of data science code, for example, a single python train.py execution.

statement: In MLflow one run holds both the metadata and the artifacts, so a result is reached through the run that made it.
quote: Each run records metadata (various information about your run such as metrics, parameters, start and end times) and artifacts (output files from the run such as model weights, images, etc).

statement: The container above a run in MLflow is the experiment, and it holds runs and logged models together.
quote: An experiment groups together runs and models for a specific task.

statement: MLflow 3 gave logged models an identity of their own: addressed by model id, no longer only through the run that produced them.
quote: MLflow 3 introduces a new model URI format that uses model IDs instead of run IDs, providing more direct model referencing

statement: MLflow's artifact store is per-run file storage: an artifact there is a file, not an object with versions of its own.
quote: Artifact store persists (typically large) artifacts for each run, such as model weights (e.g. a pickled scikit-learn model), images (e.g. PNGs), model and data files (e.g. Parquet file).

statement: Versions in MLflow come from the model registry, which is where a model name acquires a version number.
quote: you can also refer to the model through a model URI of format: models:/<model-name>/<model-version>
